positive.original:
Was soll man zu diesem Spiel noch sagen? Ich habe "erst" 2017 angefangen es zu spielen. Wollte es auf deutsch spielen, da ich zu faul war es mir selber zu übersetzen. Habe es zum ersten mal bei Youtube gesehen. Gronkh hat es damals gespielt und auf seine herrliche Art kommentiert. Habe es auch nur ein paar Folgen geschaut, damit ich nicht zu sehr gespoilert werde.
Als ich es dann angefangen habe dachte ich wirklich, dass es eine einfach Harvest Moon Kopie sein wird. 
Man lag ich Depp damals falsch. XD 
Ich habe vor kurzem meinem ersten Speicherstand mal angeguckt und dachte mir nur, man da haste aber gut was versemmelt XD.
Ich habe jetzt ein paar Tage im echten Leben in diesem Speicherstand verbracht und habe mir vorgenommen, dass erste Mal die Perfektion zu erreichen. 
Mittlerweile mit ein paar Mods, um das Leben etwas entspannter zu machen. 
Versteht mich nicht falsch, dass Spiel ist in der Vanilla Version schon klasse. Aber nach so vielen Stunden im Spiel hat man fast alles gesehen und alles gemacht. 
Ein großer Augenöffner war das Update 1.5 mit Ginger Island. Ich hatte es sehr lange nicht mehr angefasst und das Update ging voll an mir vorbei. Habe dann zufällig was gesehen und dachte mir, hä das hast du nie bei Stardew gesehen. 
Seitdem war ich dem Spiel wieder verfallen. Das 1.6 Update ist auch wieder wunderbar und das 1.7 ist ja in Arbeit. NACH 10 JAHREN. Nie wollte Eric Barone Geld für weiteren Content sehen. Das zeigt was für Herzblut in diesem Spiel steckt. Dieses Spiel ist ein Rückzugsort geworden in einer stressigen und instabilen Welt. Eine fast heile Welt, wo es zwar auch Probleme gibt, aber die zusammen gelöst werden. Wo der Mensch im Vordergrund steht. Hiermit auch ein fettes Dankeschön an Eric Barone.
Und das Schönste ist, es ist nicht alles was man zu diesem Spiel sagen und finden kann. Es gibt ein sehr geniale Modder Szene, mit richtig tollen Mods wie Stardew Valley Expanded. Diese Mod trifft den Ton des Spieles meiner Meinung nach perfekt und erweitert es sinnvoll, sodass man noch mehr haben will (deutsche Übersetzung vorhanden).
Es gibt auch ein paar sehr fragwürdige Mods die tatsächlich häufig runtergeladen wurden, ich habe da mal recherchiert. XD

Alles in allem ein tolles Spiel, man muss sich erstmal reinfuchsen, da es kein Tutorial gibt. Aber wenn man dran bleibt erwartet einen ein absolut tolles Spiel. Auf die nächsten 500 Stunden.

ALSO LASS DAS GAME BITTE SO WIE ES JETZT IST....

So nu ,was soll ich sagen, das Game hab ich erst gerade mit meiner Freundin angefangen zu Gamen, aber wer Entspannung und Ruhe in seiner Freizeit beim Spielen sucht und dem stressigen und hektischen nervösen Alltag entfliehen möchte in seiner Freizeit und gerne "Spielt", macht mit diesem Game absolut NICHTS verkehrt.....Absolut Top das Game....Es belastet auch die Hardware älterer PC's NICHT. Man hat unzählige Möglichkeiten sein eigenes " virtuelles Hofleben - Dorfleben " zu gestalten und es macht einfach nur Spaß....Und für den Preis,also kommt...da macht man nichts verkehrt....Top... und habe sehr viel Freude daran.......

positive.original:
This game has been in my life for 8 years and I have played it more than any other game. And the reason why I will never stop playing this game, is because of the love you can feel in every corner. The Music is lovely, the sprites are perfectly arragned. Every pixel is created with a love for the craft of making a game and it is visible. 
As I have played the game so often and seen (almost) everything (never done a Joja run :D ) I started playing with Mods 2 years ago and even there, you can feel that the love for this game is still in these Mods. 
ConcernedApe has created a game that spreads its love to all those, who play it and makes people create Art of it, which is the highest form of Love one can show. To create a muse for so many people and a way to connect with others is not easy, but ConcernedApe managed to do it perfectly. 

Everyone should try this game and it is for all the ages.

Thank you ConcernedApe for creating something so lovely!

positive.original:
Eines meiner Lieblingsspiele!
Egal ob Solo oder im Koop, ob Modded oder Vanilla, ich finde immer wieder zurück zu dem Spiel.

Man hat keinen Zeitdruck und genau in der Geschwindigkeit Spielen auf die man gerade Lust hat.
Die Charaktere haben eine Liebevolle Story und die Musik ist einfach nur perfekt! 
Ich lasse bei den meisten Spielen immer lieber meine eigene Musik laufen doch hier würde ich sie trotz Wiederholung niemals aus machen.

Ich kann es egal ob im Angebot oder zum Vollpreis in jedem Fall empfehlen!!

positive.original:
Ein absolut großartiges Spiel, das man nur empfehlen kann. Stardew Valley bietet eine entspannte Atmosphäre, viel Inhalt und jede Menge Möglichkeiten, seine eigene Farm aufzubauen.

Ob Farming, Angeln, Mining oder Beziehungen zu den Dorfbewohnern – hier wird es nie langweilig. Das Spiel hat einen ganz eigenen Charme und lädt immer wieder dazu ein, weiterzuspielen.

Besonders hervorzuheben ist die Liebe zum Detail und wie viel Herzblut in diesem Spiel steckt.

🎯 Fazit:
Ein zeitloses Spiel, das sowohl entspannt als auch motivierend ist und stundenlangen Spielspaß bietet.

👍 Empfehlung: Absolut empfohlen

positive.original: Stardew Valley ist ein spiel zum entspannen und ein Tolles Farm leben genießen ohne stress, es ist ein game wo man nach einen harten Tag reingeht und sich um seine Farm kümmert und seine tiere Fütter oder sich in der Stadt mit den leuten unterhält und ihre aufgaben erledigt. Und wenn man sich vom farm leben zurück ziehen will und Abenteuer erleben möchte dann kann man auch in den Minen gehen und dort Erze farmen und monster bekämpfen oder halt zu den Ingwer Inseln Reisen. in Kurz Das Game ist Perfekt zum entspannen und in Ruhe genießen des Farmer lebens :)

positive.original:
Ich habe jetzt circa 20 Stunden in Stardew Valley verbracht und bin hin- und hergerissen. Einerseits hat mich das Spiel sofort mit seinem Charme gepackt – die Grafik weckt bei mir tolle Erinnerungen an die Zeit mit dem Super Nintendo und das klassische Zelda: A Link to the Past. Es sieht fantastisch aus und die Musik ist eigentlich zum Träumen.

Aber mein persönliches Empfinden ist leider alles andere als entspannt:
Der Zeitdruck im Nacken: 
Für mich fühlt sich das Spiel oft wie ein Hamsterrad an. Wenn ich morgens um 6 Uhr anfange zu gießen und danach noch kurz in die Stadt möchte, ist der halbe Tag schon weg. Ich habe oft das Gefühl, von einem Ort zum nächsten hetzen zu müssen, nur um dann vor verschlossenen Türen zu stehen, weil die Bewohner ihre Häuser verriegeln. Diese 2-Uhr-Morgens-Deadline, bei der man einfach umkippt und Geld verliert, empfinde ich als extrem einengend.

Das Gefühl einer „To-Do-Liste“: 
Was mich persönlich am meisten stört, ist das Freundschaftssystem. Ich finde es schade, dass die mühsam aufgebauten Beziehungen wieder sinken, nur weil ich mich mal ein paar Wochen auf meine Mine oder das Angeln konzentriere. In meiner Welt bedeutet Funkstille kein aktives Schlechterwerden einer Freundschaft, sondern einfach nur Pause. Im Spiel fühlt es sich für mich aber wie eine Liste an, die ich ständig abarbeiten muss, damit nichts „rostet“. Das nimmt mir den Spaß an der eigentlichen Interaktion und stresst mich auch etwas. (Interpretiert & geschrieben von KI)

Der JOJA Markt Typ ist ein HS

I love every aspect of this game in its own unique way.

negative.original:
i dont understand how this game is universaliy loved. 
for me its just very boring and not fun at all. 
I really dont like the gameplay loop. 
its just walking around and here and there planting something or mining or talking to someone. 
and all of these parts kinda suck major balls like seriously the dialoge is so boring the cutscenes feel very incomplete and like a powerpoint presetation. 
i also think the artsytles kinda weird like its a mix between highress and low ress pixel art but in weird, like i think the world itself is pretty especially the winters but then there are just these longstrechted characters walking thru there that in my opinion just look weird and if you talk to them these pictures of there real faces just jumpscare you and stare you into your soul with there lifeless eyes.
And it just tries to be so much at once like, it tries to be a farming sim, a dungeon crawler, a muliplayer, an RPG, an story game, a ,multiplayer, a walking sim.
And in all of these parts it just falls short. 
A major point that i think was also very annoying was that theres so much loked at first, i mean i understand that certain ares should be unlocked later in the game but here you cant really do anything like you get so many quest and half of these you cant even complete cause you need an item that you only unlock 3,000 hours into the game.

I dont think this games worth a shot its just so many things mixed into one(which is ironic because i like Highgaurd and that games is some much stuff in one game) but here it just sucks. 
If you dont want to waste 14 bucks dont get this.

negative.original:
Es hat bei mir 3 Anläufe gebraucht, um dieses Spiel nicht schon wieder nach 15 min. abzuschalten. Jeder Anlauf hatte folgenden Hintergrund: "So viele positive Rezensionen, da muss was dran sein" - tatsächlich ist da auch was dran; es verleiht eine gemütliche Atmosphäre und stresst nicht. Für mich war es das aber auch schon mit den positiven Aspekten.

Stardew Valley ist unfassbar langatmig. Was als ultimatives Entspannungsspiel vorgegaugeklt wird, entpuppt sich am Ende wie ein Zweitjopb mit schlechtem Zeitmanagement. Es gibt einen großen Mangel an Ingame-Informationen, sodass auch Stardew Valley dich zu einem Wiki-Dilemma führt. Offener Browser für ständiges, externes nachschlagen im fortgeschrittenen Spiel ist auch hier angesagt, just fyi. 

Die Lauferei zu immer wieder denselben Buden nervt irgendwann nur noch, sodass ich irgendwann anfing mit /warpshop die Teleporterei zu nutzen. Das Angeln ist zu anstrengend gestaltet, weil man bei jedem Fischfang einen Balken mit Mausklicken jonglieren muss. Es nervt irgendwann nur noch und hält dich davon ab, einfach mal ne lange Angelsession zu starten. Farming an und für sich wurde clever gestaltet, ist aber auch eindeutig zu langatmig. Generell kommt man im Spiel nur sehr langsam voran, sodass der zähe Fortschritt, die schnell erloschene Energie und der rasch vergangene Tag (ingame) keinen Ansporn bieten, sondern nur noch nerven. Wer einfach chillig Säen und Ernten will, ist hier fehl am Platz. Nicht nur wegen den o.g. Aspekten, sondern auch durch das Vorhandensein von "Kämpfen" in den Minen, die durch ständige Kollisionsabfragen sich fummelig gestaltet. Wer einfach nur Materialien zum Bauen besorgen will, wird durch nervige Gegner aufgehalten. 

Das Spiel hat mehr Maloch-Charakter als man denkt. Man wird "gezwungen" das langatmige Tempo mitzumachen, aber auch den Tag möglichst optimal zu nutzen. Da muss man auch auf die Ingame-Uhrzeiten achten. Entspannung sieht also auch hier anders aus.

Die Lauferei zu immer wieder denselben Buden nervt irgendwann nur noch, sodass ich irgendwann anfing mit /warpshop die Teleporterei zu nutzen. negative.original:
*Disclaimer**
Stardew Valley is not bad. But it is probably not what you are looking for. If you are looking for a cozy or relaxing game this isn't it. This is a time management game that only rewards efficiency.

**The Issue**
For me Stardew Valley suffers from a bunch of old ideas and concepts that were created by the birthtime of the genre 20 years earlier and those turn all around the programmers missconception that a game like this needs timer. Don't get me wrong, a farming simulator needs a flow of time. How else would you know when to plant and when to harvest? But what a game like this does not need at all is a liminting ingame day that last less than 15 minutes in real time. Not if you use an Energy/Stamina system. You can't do everything at one day. You shouldn't either. That would create stress and failing would feel like you get punished. The issue is that you can reading thru the basics, going thru the menues - you know trying to figure out what you can do . and suddenly end up wasting half an ingame day with nothing because the timer is ticking. This only creates an unreasonal amount of stress in many people, once they realize that they have barely enough time to water 4 plants and talk to some villagers before they collapse.

**Why do i think that is bad**
The very premise why your character gets to that place is that you are too escaping the city life. the stress, the emptyness and the clock that ticking in your head. And what do you get? A clock ticking in your back of your neck. And again for no reason. As stated before the energy system already limits the amounts of actions you can take for a day. You could have an ingame day that could last an hour in real life time and yet wouldn't be able to do anything you can. Especially since you don't have the money yet to do much. Even if you forage food or buy it to regains energy you can't just keep on going. And even if you had enough money you couldn't stay awake forever. Eventually you will get exhausted and collapse. So my question is: why the timer at all?

**Are you doing it wrong?**
Fans of the game will tell you, that you playing it wrong. That you try to minmax, that you are stressing yourself. They are wrong. Stardew Valley is a time management assessment training and as explained before without good reason. For those that search for what the game promises - a peaceful life in the country side, a place to take a breather - the start of the game can be stressful if not punishing. Again not because of the player doing something wrong.. It is because this kind of players will only naturally react to an unneeded mechanic that is the timer. 20-25 minutes  real time for an ingame day is a gold standard since Harvest Moon. Because that was the average time a player was considered to have in one go. Be it a kid after school or a commuter in a train. That is also why you can only save in your bed. Because it allows you to prematurely end a day when your time runs out and you have to work or sleep.

**An Explanation attempt**
If you are supposed to beoffline, in a place where time stood still, but with a limiting mechanic why would you even need a timer? Because that is how you implement a fast gameplay loop. Is it necessary? No but it creates a challenge. Something some people need and seek to progress. Can i do this and this before my character collapses from exhaustion? Lets try to minmax and optimize my next day.Does that sound relaxing? It isn’t. Not for me. Probably not for a lot of people. If this sounds t you like you are working and not gaming, right? The only difference is that you are the one that is pushing yourself. Not because you want to, but because of the game triggering something you have learned. Only efficiency will be rewarded, if you are inefficient you are a failure. And for those that seek this core element of modern world within the safe confines of a game, Stardew Valley is a great game. For everyone else it is not.

**Will it be better when you progress?**
Yes. You will skill up, you will automate syour farm, you will probably make some people (or mythical creatures as it is in other games) your wageslaves. As you progress you will become more efficient, more streamlined, more a manager than a farmer. And then you will be able to make more fo the 15 minutes a day. But it will take time before you get to the stuff people like about the game. Like Socializing, exploration or crafting. A lot of time will be needed to get to that point and it won’t feel rewarding for a good amount of people. Will have a good chance to need a year to say hello to the dwindling masses of 34 citizens of Pelican Town because they will scurry around like rodents on acid while you try to find the most efficient way to spent another day of 15 minutes. Because the clock is always ticking.

**Fazit**
You love time management and efficiency and glossed over with some elements of farming and life simulation you are recommendet to buy it. If you heard that this game is cozy, you should probably reconsider. Or mod the game. There are lots of mods and that can tell you a lot already. Personally I suck at modding for 20 years now and I’m too stressed and have to little free time to spend a weekend on a mod list until a game works the way I see it should.

**Last but not least**
this all is of course colored by my own subjective opinion. Maybe you can life with what I told you. That’s great. Personally I think the genre should finally break with old standards and be more honest to itself. If you are a management simulation tell people that. Most of us older people want to relax after work and not being chained to another schedule. And it would be so easy with an option to set the timer length manually. Or simply let the energy mechanic do its work alone. Because it is already good at this.

translations.german:
*Disclaimer**
Stardew Valley is not bad. But it is probably not what you are looking for. If you are looking for a cozy or relaxing game this isn't it. This is a time management game that only rewards efficiency.

**The Issue**
For me Stardew Valley suffers from a bunch of old ideas and concepts that were created by the birthtime of the genre 20 years earlier and those turn all around the programmers missconception that a game like this needs timer. Don't get me wrong, a farming simulator needs a flow of time. How else would you know when to plant and when to harvest? But what a game like this does not need at all is a liminting ingame day that last less than 15 minutes in real time. Not if you use an Energy/Stamina system. You can't do everything at one day. You shouldn't either. That would create stress and failing would feel like you get punished. The issue is that you can reading thru the basics, going thru the menues - you know trying to figure out what you can do . and suddenly end up wasting half an ingame day with nothing because the timer is ticking. This only creates an unreasonal amount of stress in many people, once they realize that they have barely enough time to water 4 plants and talk to some villagers before they collapse.

**Why do i think that is bad**
The very premise why your character gets to that place is that you are too escaping the city life. the stress, the emptyness and the clock that ticking in your head. And what do you get? A clock ticking in your back of your neck. And again for no reason. As stated before the energy system already limits the amounts of actions you can take for a day. You could have an ingame day that could last an hour in real life time and yet wouldn't be able to do anything you can. Especially since you don't have the money yet to do much. Even if you forage food or buy it to regains energy you can't just keep on going. And even if you had enough money you couldn't stay awake forever. Eventually you will get exhausted and collapse. So my question is: why the timer at all?

**Are you doing it wrong?**
Fans of the game will tell you, that you playing it wrong. That you try to minmax, that you are stressing yourself. They are wrong. Stardew Valley is a time management assessment training and as explained before without good reason. For those that search for what the game promises - a peaceful life in the country side, a place to take a breather - the start of the game can be stressful if not punishing. Again not because of the player doing something wrong.. It is because this kind of players will only naturally react to an unneeded mechanic that is the timer. 20-25 minutes  real time for an ingame day is a gold standard since Harvest Moon. Because that was the average time a player was considered to have in one go. Be it a kid after school or a commuter in a train. That is also why you can only save in your bed. Because it allows you to prematurely end a day when your time runs out and you have to work or sleep.

**An Explanation attempt**
If you are supposed to beoffline, in a place where time stood still, but with a limiting mechanic why would you even need a timer? Because that is how you implement a fast gameplay loop. Is it necessary? No but it creates a challenge. Something some people need and seek to progress. Can i do this and this before my character collapses from exhaustion? Lets try to minmax and optimize my next day.Does that sound relaxing? It isn’t. Not for me. Probably not for a lot of people. If this sounds t you like you are working and not gaming, right? The only difference is that you are the one that is pushing yourself. Not because you want to, but because of the game triggering something you have learned. Only efficiency will be rewarded, if you are inefficient you are a failure. And for those that seek this core element of modern world within the safe confines of a game, Stardew Valley is a great game. For everyone else it is not.

**Will it be better when you progress?**
Yes. You will skill up, you will automate syour farm, you will probably make some people (or mythical creatures as it is in other games) your wageslaves. As you progress you will become more efficient, more streamlined, more a manager than a farmer. And then you will be able to make more fo the 15 minutes a day. But it will take time before you get to the stuff people like about the game. Like Socializing, exploration or crafting. A lot of time will be needed to get to that point and it won’t feel rewarding for a good amount of people. Will have a good chance to need a year to say hello to the dwindling masses of 34 citizens of Pelican Town because they will scurry around like rodents on acid while you try to find the most efficient way to spent another day of 15 minutes. Because the clock is always ticking.

**Fazit**
You love time management and efficiency and glossed over with some elements of farming and life simulation you are recommendet to buy it. If you heard that this game is cozy, you should probably reconsider. Or mod the game. There are lots of mods and that can tell you a lot already. Personally I suck at modding for 20 years now and I’m too stressed and have to little free time to spend a weekend on a mod list until a game works the way I see it should.

**Last but not least**
this all is of course colored by my own subjective opinion. Maybe you can life with what I told you. That’s great. Personally I think the genre should finally break with old standards and be more honest to itself. If you are a management simulation tell people that. Most of us older people want to relax after work and not being chained to another schedule. And it would be so easy with an option to set the timer length manually. Or simply let the energy mechanic do its work alone. Because it is already good at this.

You could have an ingame day that could last an hour in real life time and yet wouldn't be able to do anything you can. Especially since you don't have the money yet to do much. Even if you forage food or buy it to regains energy you can't just keep on going. And even if you had enough money you couldn't stay awake forever. Eventually you will get exhausted and collapse. So my question is: why the timer at all?

**Are you doing it wrong?**
Fans of the game will tell you, that you playing it wrong. That you try to minmax, that you are stressing yourself. They are wrong. Stardew Valley is a time management assessment training and as explained before without good reason. For those that search for what the game promises - a peaceful life in the country side, a place to take a breather - the start of the game can be stressful if not punishing. Again not because of the player doing something wrong.. It is because this kind of players will only naturally react to an unneeded mechanic that is the timer. 20-25 minutes  real time for an ingame day is a gold standard since Harvest Moon. Because that was the average time a player was considered to have in one go. Be it a kid after school or a commuter in a train. That is also why you can only save in your bed. Because it allows you to prematurely end a day when your time runs out and you have to work or sleep.

**An Explanation attempt**
If you are supposed to beoffline, in a place where time stood still, but with a limiting mechanic why would you even need a timer? Because that is how you implement a fast gameplay loop. Is it necessary? No but it creates a challenge. Something some people need and seek to progress. Can i do this and this before my character collapses from exhaustion? Lets try to minmax and optimize my next day.Does that sound relaxing? It isn’t. Not for me. Probably not for a lot of people. If this sounds t you like you are working and not gaming, right? The only difference is that you are the one that is pushing yourself. Not because you want to, but because of the game triggering something you have learned. Only efficiency will be rewarded, if you are inefficient you are a failure. And for those that seek this core element of modern world within the safe confines of a game, Stardew Valley is a great game. For everyone else it is not.

**Will it be better when you progress?**
Yes. You will skill up, you will automate syour farm, you will probably make some people (or mythical creatures as it is in other games) your wageslaves. As you progress you will become more efficient, more streamlined, more a manager than a farmer. And then you will be able to make more fo the 15 minutes a day. But it will take time before you get to the stuff people like about the game. Like Socializing, exploration or crafting. A lot of time will be needed to get to that point and it won’t feel rewarding for a good amount of people. Will have a good chance to need a year to say hello to the dwindling masses of 34 citizens of Pelican Town because they will scurry around like rodents on acid while you try to find the most efficient way to spent another day of 15 minutes. Because the clock is always ticking.

**Fazit**
You love time management and efficiency and glossed over with some elements of farming and life simulation you are recommendet to buy it. If you heard that this game is cozy, you should probably reconsider. Or mod the game. There are lots of mods and that can tell you a lot already. Personally I suck at modding for 20 years now and I’m too stressed and have to little free time to spend a weekend on a mod list until a game works the way I see it should.

**Last but not least**
this all is of course colored by my own subjective opinion. Maybe you can life with what I told you. That’s great. Personally I think the genre should finally break with old standards and be more honest to itself. If you are a management simulation tell people that. Most of us older people want to relax after work and not being chained to another schedule. And it would be so easy with an option to set the timer length manually. Or simply let the energy mechanic do its work alone. Because it is already good at this.
